source.title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems

accepted.question_text: For geometric curvature energies on curves, can one prove additional regularity beyond the fractional Sobolev regularity that characterizes the energy spaces for local minimizers or critical points of the tangent-point energy, defined by integrating the inverse p-th power of the tangent-point radius between pairs of points on a curve, or of integral Menger curvature, defined by integrating the inverse p-th power of the circumradius over triples of points on a curve? If such extra regularity exists, does the optimal regularity depend on the exponent p, what happens to that p-dependent regularity as p tends to infinity, and does that limiting behavior give new information about the still-open optimal regularity of ideal knots?
accepted.context_brief: Regularity of critical points for curve energies

Open questions 2.2.3. Despite degeneracies in the non-local Euler-Lagrange equations, is there any chance to prove additional regularity (beyond the fractional Sobolev regularity characterising energy spaces) for local minimisers or critical points of tangent-point energies (2.1.7), or of integral Menger curvature (2.1.5)? Does the optimal regularity depend on p, and if yes, what happens with that p-dependent regularity in the limit p → ∞? Does that lead to new insights into the still open optimal regularity of ideal knots?

accepted.question_text: For higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies on submanifolds, including higher-dimensional integral Menger curvature and tangent-point energy, what are the Euler-Lagrange equations, can one prove higher regularity for local minimizers or critical points, and what variational inclusions should replace Euler-Lagrange equations for the nonsmooth geometric energies obtained by replacing some of the integrations with maximizations? The same block also asks what regularity can be proved for thick knotted surfaces that minimize area.

Open questions 2.2.4. What are the Euler-Lagrange-equations for higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies like integral Menger curvature (2.1.5) or tangent-point energies (2.1.10)? Is there any chance to prove higher regularity of local minimisers or critical points of these energies? What form do the expected variational inclusions have for the non-smooth geometric energies (2.1.3), (2.1.15), (2.1.16)? What can be said about the regularity of thick knotted surfaces minimising area?

accepted.question_text: For geometric curvature energies on nonsmooth sets in arbitrary dimension, can Meurer’s rectifiability theorem be extended from his integrand KM to the integrands used here for integral Menger curvature or to tangent-point energies, and if so on what suitably broad class of nonsmooth sets? The authors also ask how Meurer’s rectifiability result is related to other recent rectifiability criteria.

Open questions 2.2.8. Can one extend Meurer’s rectifiability result to the integrands (2.1.9) or (2.1.12) of integral Menger curvature or to the tangent-point energies (2.1.10) defined on a suitable wide class of non-smooth sets? How does Meurer’s result relate to other recent rectifiability results like [127, 7]?

accepted.question_text: In the scale-invariant regime for geometric curvature energies, what is the optimal regularity of finite-energy Lipschitz curves or submanifolds? For a higher-dimensional generalization of Möbius energy, how regular are finite-energy submanifolds? What are the optimal constants in Fenchel-type theorems that bound the energy needed to close a curve or a surface? And if a k-dimensional manifold immersed in R^n has finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy or finite scale-invariant integral Menger curvature, must its image automatically be embedded?

evidence.quote: The scale-invariant exponent for integral Menger curvature Mp(Σ) on two-dimensional surfaces Σ ⊂ R3 is p = 8, and we proved a Fenchel-type theorem [120, Theorem 1.2].

Open questions 2.2.10. What is the optimal regularity of finite energy Lipschitz curves or submanifolds for any of the geometric curvature energies in the scale-invariant case? How regular are submanifolds of finite energy for a suitable generalisation of the Möbius energy to higher dimensional objects? How much geometric curvature energy does one really need to close a curve or a surface, in other words what are the optimal constants in Fenchel-type theorems like Theorem 2.2.9? Is every k-dimensional manifold Mk immersed in Rn automatically embedded if its image has finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy E2k (see (2.1.10)), or finite scale-invariant integral Menger curvature Mk(k+2) (see (2.1.11))?

accepted.question_text: Beyond the known global minimizers, do geometric curvature energies admit other critical points in each prescribed knot class? In particular, are there critical unknots distinct from the round circle, how many such critical configurations can occur, can critical points for different geometric curvature energies be related to one another for example by Γ-convergence, what can be proved about their stability, and can critical configurations be found in higher dimensions?
accepted.context_brief: Existence and stability of nonminimal critical points

evidence.quote: Existence of critical points. For all geometric curvature energies above scale-invariance one can find (at least one) minimising knot in a given isotopy class.

Open questions 2.2.11. Are there critical points for geometric curvature energies in every prescribed knot class other than the known global minimisers? In particular, are there critical unknots different from the round circle? And if so, how many are there? Can we relate critical points of different geometric curvature energies with each other, e.g., via Γ-convergence? What can be said about the stability of such critical points? Is it possible to find critical configurations in higher dimensions?

accepted.question_text: Does the round circle minimize integral Menger curvature for curves? More broadly, can one determine the actual shapes of ideal knots, of links with more than two components that minimize Möbius energy, and of global minimizers for other geometric curvature energies on curves? For elastic knots, what can be proved about nontrivial knot classes other than the (2,b)-torus knots, and what is the shape of twisted elastic knots?
accepted.context_brief: Shapes of curve minimizers and elastic knots

evidence.quote: Open questions 2.2.13. Does the round circle minimise integral Menger curvature (2.1.5)? Can one prove more about the actual shape of ideal knots? What is the shape of links with more than two components minimising the Möbius energy? Can one identify the shapes of global minimisers of other geometric curvature energies for curves? What can be said about elastic knots for non-trivial knot classes different from (2, b)-torus knots? What is the shape of twisted elastic knots?

accepted.question_text: For higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies, can one identify the shapes of global minimizers? In the isotopy-finiteness theorem for submanifolds with bounded integral Menger curvature, what is the optimal constant controlling the number of isotopy types under a given energy bound? Are there meaningful topological invariants or geometric quantities for higher-dimensional knots that can be controlled by higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? Do higher-dimensional elastic knots exist, for example as minimizers of the Willmore functional in prescribed isotopy classes, and if they do, can one say anything about their shapes?
accepted.context_brief: Higher-dimensional minimizers, invariants, and elastic knots

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.2.15 (Isotopy finiteness). Let E, d > 0 be given. Then there are at most K = K(E, d, k, n, p) different ambient isotopy types among all k-dimensional Lipschitz submanifolds Σ ⊂ Rn with integral Menger curvature Mp(Σ) ≤ E and diam Σ ≤ d.

Open questions 2.2.16. Is it possible to identify the shape of global minimisers of higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? The explicit constant in Theorem 2.2.15 is far from being optimal, what is the best constant bounding the number of isotopy types under given energy values? For curves the energies could often be related to knot invariants or to quantities like the average crossing number (2.1.17) controlling knot invariants. Are there meaningful topological invariants or geometric quantities for higher-dimensional knots that could be controlled by means of higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies? Are there higher-dimensional elastic knots, for instance minimisers of the Willmore functional in arbitrary prescribed isotopy classes? And can one say anything about their shapes?
